rst31-hygiene2-noro-source-scope.title: Do not confuse the scope of “about eight-tenths”
rst31-hygiene2-noro-source-scope.text: The textbook’s “about 80%” does not mean that 80% of food handlers are infected. A similar explanation appears in MHLW’s 10 November 2017 notice, concerning norovirus food poisoning and food contamination via cooking workers. The textbook’s original statistical dataset has not been established, so do not substitute current all-food-poisoning or individual-store proportions. Explain continued contamination prevention through pre-work health checks and appropriate handwashing.

rst31-hygiene2-link-noro-2017.title: Check the 2017 notice on the official page
rst31-hygiene2-link-noro-2017.text: Check MHLW’s notice from that time to preserve its scope and date when explaining it.

rst31-hygiene2-q049.objective: Distinguish percentage scope and source date
rst31-hygiene2-q049.stem: Which reading of “about eight-tenths” in MHLW’s 2017 notice is appropriate?
options: About eight-tenths of surveyed workers were infected with norovirus
In 2026 every store’s norovirus food-poisoning proportion must still be about eight-tenths
About eight-tenths of all food poisoning was caused by norovirus
It describes frequent food contamination via workers in norovirus food poisoning
reasons: This confuses causal routes with worker infection prevalence.
This treats a 2017 explanation as a fixed 2026 store value.
This expands causes within norovirus food poisoning to causes of all food poisoning.
This preserves scope/causal route and connects to health checks/handwashing.
rst31-hygiene2-q049.explanation: The scope is norovirus food poisoning and contamination via workers, not worker infection prevalence or all-food-poisoning causes, nor a guarantee for current individual stores.

rst31-integration-q001.objective: Link pectoral, pelvic and anal fins to the source’s general fish diagram.
rst31-integration-q001.stem: In that diagram, which sequence matches behind the gill cover, front underside and rear underside?
reasons: This swaps front/rear underside fins.
This swaps behind-gill and rear-underside names.
All three names match the illustrated positions.
This reverses pectoral and pelvic positions.
rst31-integration-q001.explanation: The general diagram places pectoral fins behind gill covers, pelvic fins at the front underside and anal fins at the rear underside. Do not ignore species variation and assert this for every fish.

rst31-integration-q002.objective: Combine general hygiene and important-process controls in plans and communicate implementation.
rst31-integration-q002.stem: The manager plans only critical heating, leaving cleaning/handwashing to individuals. Which improvement fits?
options: Only managers read plans; staff see only results
Heating records make cleaning/handwashing plans and communication unnecessary
Include general hygiene and check staff can explain work/abnormality reporting
Plan only cleaning and leave heating to experience
reasons: Communication to implementing staff is missing.
Important-process controls do not remove general hygiene.
This combines controls and checks understanding/implementation.
General hygiene cannot replace important-process controls.
rst31-integration-q002.explanation: HACCP-based management combines both and communicates plans for implementation; documents alone are insufficient.

rst31-integration-q003.objective: Distinguish voluntary-recall decisions from notification checks.
rst31-integration-q003.stem: A relevant food recall begins. Someone says voluntary recalls need no notification. Which judgement fits?
options: All voluntary recalls need none, regardless of food/reason
Separate recall and notification decisions; check scope/conditions with managers/health authorities
Keep serving suspect food normally until notification checks finish
Treat every return identically and omit food/reason records
reasons: The name voluntary alone cannot establish exemption.
This separates decisions/notification and checks individual conditions.
Prevent health harm during checks; this does not justify normal service.
Food/reason records support checks/communication; not every return is identical.
rst31-integration-q003.explanation: Starting a voluntary recall and checking statutory notification are separate. Check scope/exceptions and record food, reasons and action; do not assume voluntary means exempt.

rst31-integration-q004.objective: Distinguish food-hygiene supervisor duties from operator direction/responsibility.
rst31-integration-q004.stem: An operator appoints a food-hygiene supervisor. Which role fits?
options: The supervisor manages hygiene under operator direction and shares issues
Appointment removes the operator from hygiene management
Operator instructions mean the supervisor need not perform hygiene work
The supervisor withholds known hygiene problems
reasons: This combines supervisor practice and operator role.
Appointment does not free the operator from involvement.
Receiving directions does not remove implementation duties.
Unshared problems do not lead to necessary improvements.
rst31-integration-q004.explanation: The supervisor follows operator direction. Appointment does not eliminate operator responsibility; share hygiene opinions/issues.

rst31-integration-q005.objective: Check everyday infection prevention and self-protection during vomit/faeces cleanup.
rst31-integration-q005.stem: A cook cleans family vomit at home. Which matches prevention principles?
options: Gloves eliminate infection risk, so other measures need no check
Home infection is unrelated to work; bare hands are fine
Take care at home too, using disposable mask/gloves/apron for protection
Wear dirty work clothes to prevent home infection
reasons: Gloves alone do not eliminate infection possibility.
Home infection can make food handlers contamination sources.
This combines home prevention with specified self-protection.
Dirty workwear is not prevention and may spread contamination.
rst31-integration-q005.explanation: Food handlers guard against infection in everyday/home life. Disposable mask/gloves/apron protect during faeces/vomit cleanup; detailed methods/chemicals require separate checking.

rst31-integration-q007.objective: Connect hospitality with concrete considerate actions and repeated practice.
rst31-integration-q007.stem: A newcomer says hospitality needs feeling but no movement practice. Which advice fits?
options: Repeatedly practise clean, kind, courteous actions expressing care
Identical actions for everyone remove the need to ask wishes
Continue unwanted help to look kind
reasons: This connects intention/action and basic-skill learning.
Basic actions still require checking wishes.
Intentions do not justify omitting cleanliness/courtesy.
Ignoring preferences is not caring for someone.
rst31-integration-q007.explanation: Express consideration in concrete actions, learning/practising basics and checking circumstances/wishes. This is not attributing one trait to nationalities/groups.

rst31-integration-q008.objective: Understand accumulated small dissatisfactions and enquire early.
rst31-integration-q008.stem: Repeated short waits and insufficient explanations precede a strong complaint. Which response fits?
options: Only the last incident must matter; ignore earlier events
Consider accumulated small dissatisfactions and ask carefully what was wrong
Short individual waits cannot accumulate dissatisfaction
Judge personality alone without checking explanations/service
reasons: Earlier circumstances may matter, not just the final incident.
Treat accumulation as a possibility and verify through the guest’s account.
Short waits combined with poor explanations can increase dissatisfaction.
Personality assumptions alone miss service problems.
rst31-integration-q008.explanation: Several small dissatisfactions can precede a complaint. Do not assume one cause; listen and establish circumstances.
